title: AccountsAPI — v1 Never Went Away
objective: The current API version correctly stops you from reading another account. Find the old version that's still running.

verifier.condition: An account record belonging to a different signed-in user than the caller is returned by the v1 endpoint, while the equivalent v2 request for the same account correctly refuses it.

weakness: An authorization check added to fix an old vulnerability was only added to the current API version; the previous version, kept mounted for backwards compatibility, still has the original, unfixed behavior.
seededData: Users alice and bob, each with an account record. In-memory.

credentials.label: User account
credentials.note: Try your own account id on both API versions first.

hints: Read your own account through both /api/v1/ and /api/v2/ and confirm they return the same thing for your own data.
Now try bob's account id through v2 — it should be refused. Try the exact same id through v1.
Old API versions are often kept running for compatibility long after a fix ships to the current one.
burpNotes: Repeat the same account-id request against both /api/v1/accounts/:id and /api/v2/accounts/:id and diff the responses.
